raw:
{
  "need": "Autonomy",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "show": "Every reset of the curfew has felt like a negotiation they won, which now reads to them as proof the rule is soft and their judgment outranks yours." },
  "read": "They are testing whether the boundary is real or just a suggestion, and each successful push has taught them that persistence pays off. Underneath that is a genuine developmental pull toward self-governance — they need to feel like someone whose choices are trusted, not just managed.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lock the curfew down hard and take away privileges until they comply — which signals you've finally lost patience but doesn't give them any ownership, so they dig in or scheme around it." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the line firmly on the time itself while handing them real agency over how they earn an extension — turn the standard from something imposed on them into something they can grow into.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The curfew time is not up for debate tonight or next week.",
    "Every violation has a real, same-night consequence — no exceptions, no renegotiation in the moment.",
    "Two resets have already happened; there is no third reset, only an earned path forward."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let them propose what a responsible track record looks like over the next month that would justify a later time.",
    "Let them choose how they check in when they're out — a text, a call, a location share — so the method is theirs.",
    "Allow the occasional planned exception if they ask in advance, which rewards forethought rather than after-the-fact excuses."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 4, "label": "Choices" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I want to talk about curfew and I'm not coming in hot. I know you're at an age where a fixed time feels like I'm treating you like you're twelve, and I get that it's frustrating." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "What I genuinely want to understand is what's been happening on the nights it slips — because I don't think you're just blowing me off. What's actually going on out there that makes the time hard to hit?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's where I land: the time we have right now stays put, because we've moved it twice and the pattern isn't working for either of us. But I'm not interested in just policing you forever. Tell me what you think earning a later curfew would actually look like — I want to hear your version of it, because you know your life better than I do." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm holding this standard because I have high expectations for you, and I genuinely believe you can handle them — that's not me saying you've failed, it's me saying you're capable of more consistency than we've seen lately. So let's write down what you just said and make it the actual plan. Starting now, no slipping and no excuses in the moment. And if you're ever stuck somewhere and need help, you call me — that part never changes." }
  ],
  "longGame": "What you're building here is not just a curfew habit — it's the moment they learn that trustworthiness is a currency they control. Every time they hit the mark without being chased, they bank credibility, and you keep rewarding it with real latitude. That's the loop you want running through the rest of their teenage years and into their twenties."
}
situation: Curfew keeps slipping later and the excuses pile up. We have already reset it twice.
